title: Week Summary: Performance and Scalability Perspective

concepts.name: Performance scenario
concepts.description: A quality scenario that specifies workload, environment, response, and measurable performance target.

concepts.name: Latency budget
concepts.description: An allocation of acceptable response time across elements in an end-to-end path.

concepts.name: Throughput
concepts.description: The amount of work a system can complete in a given period under specified conditions.

concepts.name: Workload model
concepts.description: A description of expected requests, users, data size, arrival patterns, and operating conditions.

concepts.name: Scalability
concepts.description: The ability of a system to maintain acceptable service as workload or data volume grows.

concepts.name: Horizontal scaling
concepts.description: Adding more instances or nodes to increase capacity rather than making one node larger.

concepts.name: Caching
concepts.description: Storing reusable data closer to consumers to reduce latency, load, or repeated computation.

concepts.name: Partitioning
concepts.description: Dividing data, work, or responsibility across multiple elements to improve scale or isolation.

concepts.name: Performance evidence
concepts.description: A measurement, analysis, test, or prototype result supporting a performance claim.

concepts.name: Capacity model
concepts.description: A model estimating how resources, workload, and architecture determine system capacity.

concepts.name: Load test
concepts.description: A test that exercises the system under expected or extreme workload to observe performance behavior.

concepts.name: Optimization tradeoff
concepts.description: A design compromise introduced when improving performance affects cost, complexity, reliability, or other qualities.
